answer: An agent registry assigns consecutive global serials k and locks kB coins per live credential, where B is a fixed positive amount. With n existing identities, the next requires at least (n+1)B. Each bond backs exactly one credential; splitting wallets cannot share it, and deleting identities never rewinds the counter. Handles such as willow, ember and comet gain no age discount: pre-aging n aliases in parallel still ties up at least Bn(n+1)/2 coins.
